ledger.claim: The platform's own record establishes the deviation the rider complains of: trip_record.actual_distance_km is 8.3 km against trip_record.optimal_distance_km of 7.3 km, a deviation of 1.00 km under POL-RD-22's subtraction, and the recommended route ran via Seletar Road while the vehicle went by Yio Chu Kang Road and Jalan Kayu. The rider's account - 'at least 1 km more' - is therefore not an assertion that needs corroboration from elsewhere; it is the platform's own figure.

The driver's counterstatement that the distance was 'about the same' is contradicted by the record it comes from. The trip record logs a route_deviation_detected at Yishun Avenue 1 / Yio Chu Kang Road and a route_rejoined at Sengkang West Avenue / Jalan Kayu, and the GPS trace runs on Yio Chu Kang Road and Jalan Kayu from 13:27:45 to 13:35:45, on a route the record itself describes as recommended via Seletar Road. The deviation is a recorded fact of this trip, not a matter of the rider's impression.

There is no traffic justification for leaving the recommended route. The LTA traffic artifact covering the recommended segment - Seletar Road, Yishun Avenue 1 to Sengkang West Avenue, both directions, valid 12:51 to 14:21 and so overlapping the trip window - records no incident, roadwork or closure, with speed bands 5-6, and the derived result is justifies_reroute false with type NONE; the artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and was retrieved by the platform rather than supplied by a party. POL-RD-23 makes congestion, an incident or a closure the only justifications, and it says in terms that a driver's assertion with no such data does not justify a reroute - which is all the driver offers here ('Jalan Kayu road is smoother'). Rows (a), (b) and (c) of POL-RD-24 are therefore unavailable to the driver.

The driver also never told the rider he was leaving the recommended route. The chat log for this trip carries 0 messages and the trip record lists no in-app calls, and no call recording is in the record at all. POL-RD-21 requires notice by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation - a brief reason is enough, but something is required - and a verbal notice with no recording cannot be established. Nothing in this record shows the rider agreed to the longer route, so the 'rider informed and agreed' limb of POL-RD-24 never opens and the rider's objection stands unaddressed by the driver.

The rider paid for the extra kilometre rather than merely observing it: the trip was metered on distance, with distance_charged_km of 8.3 at the 0.72 SGD per-km rate producing a distance fare of 5.98 SGD inside the 12.65 SGD total, while the recommended route was 7.3 km. The disputed sum is the excess distance the deviation added to the meter, and the rider's claim is directed at exactly that.

If the deviation is found to be over the 1.0 km tolerance, POL-RD-24(d) applies and the excess distance fare is refunded in full: the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, 1.00 x 0.72 = 0.72 SGD. That 0.72 SGD, not the 2.50 SGD named in the claim, is the clause's own measure of the excess, and under POL-GEN-03 a partial refund is read against the filing party - here the rider - so it is the rider and not the driver who stops carrying that charge.

The rider does not ask the judge to re-measure the route; he asks that the outcome not be inferred from the very edge of a tolerance. The deviation the record yields is 1.00 km - the difference of two figures the trip record states only to one decimal place, 7.3 and 8.3 - and it sits exactly on POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so whether POL-RD-24(d) or (e) governs depends on a boundary the record's own precision does not resolve. That is the situation POL-GEN-26 addresses: where the fact a rule needs cannot be established, the case is escalated with the open question stated rather than decided on the edge of tolerance. On escalation no money issues and the amount is held rather than collected, so the rider is not left carrying the disputed charge while a human reviews which side of the tolerance this trip fell on.

The deviation is measured from the platform's own recorded distances, as POL-RD-22 requires: trip_record.actual_distance_km 8.3 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 7.3 km = 1.00 km, and POL-RD-22 provides that a deviation of 1.0 km or less is within tolerance. On POL-RD-24's matrix that is row (e) - not traffic-justified, deviation 1 km or less - which yields no refund, so the rider's claim for 2.50 SGD fails at the first arithmetic step.

The rider's assertion of 'at least 1 km more' is not a case for a refund: the refund rows of POL-RD-24 are gated on a deviation over 1 km, and the recorded deviation sits exactly on the 1.0 km tolerance line, which POL-RD-22 reads as within tolerance. Being on the tolerance line is not a partial entitlement - rows (c) and (e) both pay nothing.

The chat log carries 0 messages and the trip record carries no in-app calls, so the record cannot show the driver informed the rider of the deviation under POL-RD-21. That point does not decide the money here: POL-RD-24's refund rows turn on traffic justification and deviation distance, and row (e) - a deviation of 1 km or less, not traffic-justified - pays nothing whether or not notice was given.

The only traffic data in evidence is the LTA advisory for Seletar Road, which is of type NONE with speed bands 5-6 over the trip window. POL-RD-23 accepts only congestion, an incident or a closure on the recommended segment as justification, and expressly says a driver's bare assertion of traffic does not justify a reroute; the driver's 'Jalan Kayu is smoother' explanation is such an assertion. That fixes the case in row (e) of POL-RD-24 rather than row (b), and no refund follows either way.

The driver-device GPS trace is complete - 34 fixes at 30 s intervals from 13:21:15 to 13:37:45, coverage 100%, no gaps and no interval over 120 s - and it shows a single departure from the recommended route onto Yio Chu Kang Road and a rejoin at Sengkang West Avenue, exactly the one deviation the trip record logs. POL-RD-22 uses the trace to show which route was taken and when, and not to re-measure distance, so the trace cannot enlarge the 1.00 km figure.

Even if a refund were owed, the rider's 2.50 SGD figure is not the policy measure. Under POL-RD-24 the excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the base per-km rate without surge: 1.00 km x 0.72 SGD = 0.72 SGD, not 2.50 SGD. The fare ledger confirms the trip was charged at 12.65 SGD with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00, so no part of the charge has been returned.

NO_ACTION is party-relative under POL-GEN-03 and never means 'restore a charge'. Here the rider filed and the present state is that the fare stands as charged - 12.65 SGD, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 - so leaving the state untouched returns nothing to the rider and leaves the driver the fare for a trip that was in fact performed. That is the driver's win on this record.

No escalation is required and an AI ruling may stand: the deviation of 1.00 km is inside POL-RD-25's 2 km limb, and the dispute value of 2.50 SGD is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence, with no fraud flag on either profile to raise the bar to 0.95. The facts the governing row needs - the recorded distances and the advisory type - are both carried by complete artifacts, so POL-GEN-26 does not open a question either.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the rider filed this dispute asking for 2.50 SGD back, saying the driver took Yio Chu Kang Road and Jalan Kayu instead of Seletar Road. The platform's own trip record (EV-TRIP-05007) settles the distance. It records the actual route at 8.3 km against the recommended route via Seletar Road at 7.3 km. Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is the difference between those two recorded figures — 8.3 minus 7.3 = 1.00 km — and POL-RD-22 provides that a deviation of 1.0 km or less is within tolerance. So the deviation here is 1.00 km, which is on the tolerance line and therefore within it. Turning to POL-RD-24's matrix, the reroute was not traffic-justified: the only traffic data in evidence (EV-ADVIS-05007-01) covers Seletar Road over the trip window and is of type NONE with speed bands 5-6, so it records no incident, roadwork or closure, and the driver's explanation that 'Jalan Kayu road is smoother' is not one of the justifications POL-RD-23 names. That places the case in row (e) of POL-RD-24 — not traffic-justified, deviation 1 km or less — which pays no refund, the deviation being within tolerance. The driver is right that no refund is due, though not for the reason he gave: the record does show a real deviation (the trace runs on Yio Chu Kang Road and Jalan Kayu from 13:27:45 to 13:35:45), it is simply too small to trigger a refund. The rider is also right that the driver never told him about the reroute — the chat log (EV-CHAT-05007) carries 0 messages and there is no call recording — but that affects rows (a)-(c) of POL-RD-24, not row (e), which pays nothing whether or not notice was given. Two rider points are declined. First, the suggestion that the case should be escalated under POL-GEN-26 because the deviation sits exactly on the 1.0 km boundary: POL-RD-22 fixes the deviation as the difference of the platform's recorded distances, both of which are present, complete (weight 1.0) and give exactly 1.00 km, so the fact the rule needs is established and nothing is left open — the policy's own words, '1.0 km or less is within tolerance', resolve the boundary. Second, the alternative that a refund of 0.72 SGD is owed: that figure is the correct measure of the excess distance fare had a refund been triggered (1.00 km x the 0.72 SGD per-km rate in EV-FARE-05007), not the 2.50 SGD claimed, but no refund is triggered because the deviation is within tolerance. The rider's claim is therefore not supported and the present state stands: the metered fare of 12.65 SGD charged to the rider (refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is left as is. The deviation is 1.00 km, well inside POL-RD-25's 2 km AI limit, and the disputed value of 2.50 SGD is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so this AI ruling is final and no escalation or referral arises.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
